title: Verbal Ability
description: Grammar, vocabulary and reading skills for the English section.

topics.title: Tenses and agreement
topics.description: Use the right verb form for every subject and time.

lessons.title: Subject-verb agreement
lessons.objective: Match verbs to their subjects, even in tricky sentences.

activities.title: Singular subject, singular verb
activities.body: In the simple present, a singular subject (he, she, it, or one person or thing) takes a verb ending in -s. A plural subject does not.
activities.example:
The boy plays football.
The boys play football.

activities.title: Watch out for tricky subjects
activities.body: Each, every and everyone are singular. Ignore the words between the subject and the verb: find the real subject first.
activities.example:
Each of the students has a book.
The box of pens is on the desk.

activities.hint: What is on the table: the list, or the items?
activities.explanation: The subject is "list", which is singular. "Of items" is just extra detail.
Everyone is singular, so it takes has.
Parents is plural, so the verb has no -s: my parents live.

questions.explanation: Neither is singular, so it takes is.
With she, the simple present negative is doesn't + verb.
The subject is books, which is plural. On the shelf is extra detail.
